sections.text:
1 Opusculum Esdrae de diebus faustis et infaustis saepissime invenitur e. g. in
Parisino 22, s. XII, f. 277 (cf. Omont, Inventaire, IV, p. 61). Kalandologium vel
brontologium Esdrae prophetae tributum exstat in Parisin. 3028, f. 163v, cf. 2286,
f. 110r. Inter sacrae artis auctores Esdram eundem reperimus (cf. Berthelot, La
chimie au moyen âge, 1893, t. II, p. 294). — De Pseudo-Esdrae apocalypsibus, cf.
Schürer, Gesch. Jüd. Volkes, III3, p. 245; Duval, Littérature syriaque, 1899, p. 93;
Basset, Les apocryphes éthiopiens, t. IX, 1899. F. C.
sections.en: 1 The little work of Ezra concerning auspicious and inauspicious days is very often found, e.g., in Parisinus 22, 12th c., f. 277 (cf. Omont, Inventaire, IV, p. 61). A calendrology or brontology attributed to the prophet Ezra exists in Parisin. 3028, f. 163v, cf. 2286, f. 110r. Among the authors of the sacred art we find the same Ezra (cf. Berthelot, La chimie au moyen âge, 1893, t. II, p. 294). — Concerning the apocalypses of Pseudo-Ezra, cf. Schürer, Gesch. Jüd. Volkes, III3, p. 245; Duval, Littérature syriaque, 1899, p. 93; Basset, Les apocryphes éthiopiens, t. IX, 1899. F. C.

summary.headline: Astrological Texts in the Venetian Codex
summary.text: Catalogue of astrological and mathematical texts in a Venetian codex, listing works on the solar sphere and monthly diet, observation of the seven stars, Egyptian month names, Esdras’s auspicious days, Hephaestio’s twelve parts, Stephen the Philosopher’s defense of mathematical art, stellar causation, apogee and perigee, and Hermes Trismegistus’s twelve places. Authorities and editions cited include Camerarius, John of Damascus, Hephaestio of Thebes, Stephen the Philosopher, Hermes Trismegistus, Migne, and Engelbrecht.
